cases.issues: The pelican remains recognizable, but the upright pose and absent flowing scarf lose some of the baseline gesture. Brick-built wheels are a valid treatment; bicycle joints remain uncertain. Finishing permission has produced more stepped anatomy, without a clear overall visual improvement.

The taller head, fuller body and stepped facial colour pattern read more clearly as the character than the compressed baseline. Deliberate brick sculpture works on the front; the rear remains a broad dark rectangular wall, and the final 1173 parts still exceed the soft target range.

The dock scene remains coherent, but the chunky brick-built tyres and heavier wheel/frame proportions make the bicycle less convincing than the baseline spoked-wheel version. Purposeful studs are valid; the baseline tiled timber dock has clearer material separation. Attachment uncertainty remains.

The stepped head and face read more clearly as the character and the body is less overwhelmed by a tall rectangular hood. Dark flippers and broad rear panels remain simplified; the new 1318-part build is substantially above its 1000-part target. The visible front improvement therefore has a budget qualification.

The separated hall and pagoda remain recognizable with a connecting route. Roofs are more sharply angular and the ensemble is plainer; the pagoda still dominates. Coherent brick/roof treatment is valid, but there is no clear overall improvement over the baseline.

The compact pond/bridge/gate arrangement is a useful alternative to the broad straight canal. Grey roofs are more angular and less graceful than the baseline black eaves; scene cohesion remains good, with no clear overall gain across form, finish and views.

Brick-built patterned wings visibly meet the shoulder/body instead of hovering above it. The creature and long tail read more coherently across views, and the stepped wing outlines are deliberate. Thin planar wings, a blocky face and remaining diagnostics still limit confidence; no physical-buildability claim.

The longer body, shaped tail and patterned swept wings read more coherently across views. Wing roots are closer to the torso than the baseline detached-looking panels, although contact and support remain uncertain. The small treasure platform and path leave the subject dominant; the face and wings remain fairly planar.

The broad triangular hull is clearer and less dominated by the stepped dorsal tower. The moon and secondary craft give the display a more coherent space composition. The moon is a flat mosaic and the dorsal terraces are still repetitive, but the ship reads better from front and top at a similar part count.

The clean standalone orange-and-blue craft has a coherent material treatment, but almost all Ewok identity is reduced to timber cladding. Trees, huts, elevated routes and forest activity disappear, so the thematic blend is much weaker than the baseline treeport. A similar total masks the tradeoff between a more self-contained assembly and worse brief fidelity; I prefer the baseline.

Both builds have a continuous tapered hull, compact supports and readable engine clusters. The candidate is a little cleaner at the centreline but still has repeated studded hull terraces and dense surface machinery. Similar counts and four-angle quality make this a near tie, rather than a clear prompt improvement.

The two huts and connecting bridge keep the forest/space scene recognizable, but tall nearly cylindrical trunks and thin foliage rings look less like trees than the baseline layered crown. The elevated ship and brick-built figures provide activity but lose some of the baseline character and finish. The rear exposes the repetitive trunk treatment especially clearly. The baseline is preferred overall.

note: All four angles reviewed. Deliberate pixel/stepped forms and purposeful studs are valid. Scores are subjective single-sample assessments, not physical certification or causal proof.
